explanation: Fires on the continuation token of a familiar multi-token word or fixed phrase whose earlier part makes it highly predictable (shopping -> ' cart', bottom -> ' line', st -> 'ents', ECMAS -> 'cript', Greg -> 'ory', \include -> 'graphics'). The examples cover many unrelated domains and no single topic, so the only common thread is that the token completes something predictable.

Fires on an early subword piece of a rare proper name or unusual word that is split into several tokens, mostly surnames and place names (' Os'+orio, ' Port'+man, 'As'+'im'+ov, 'Bed'+norz, ' Shim'+ashki, ' DeV'+one). Common whole words do not trigger it.

A mixture: deictic or definite references to a nation, party or team ('the party', 'United States of America', 'this country', 'the Lady Bears'), the newline after the party line in US court case captions ('Defendant-Appellant.\n'), plus scattered name fragments and URL pieces.

Top examples are assorted function words, nouns and punctuation in ordinary prose and code ('Just do', 'To activate', 'de lo', 'By the', '#include <stdio.h>\n'), with no shared token or context that I can find.

Fires on a word-initial subword fragment made of a consonant cluster when the word is split into several tokens, above all ' cr' (cradles, crumpled, crickets, cranes, crates, craves), and also ' cl', ' ch', ' anch', ' lanc'. Whole words and later fragments fire weakly or not at all.

Strongest on GNU/GPL license boilerplate: ' with' in 'along with this program' and ' not' in 'if not, write to the Free Software Foundation'. Weaker, scattered hits on predictable verbs and particles in prose ('By using this website', 'still active', 'all over', 'part of').

Mostly words about light, imaging and photography: ' light', ' camera', ' sun', ' video', 'raction', ' weather', ' Film Editing', image '.convert'. It also has some unrelated strong hits (' to' after a company name, ' enables', ' chef').

Fires on tokens made of, or starting with, the letter t/T (Latin, Cyrillic or Greek), especially a lone 't'/'T' fragment that begins a word split into pieces ('T'+ikl, ' t'+iga, 'T'+ucson), and on 'ot'/'lot'/'iot' pieces inside words such as normotensive, genotyped and haplotypes.

Fires on the second element of a fixed compound, set phrase or camelCase identifier, where the first part predicts it: 'Sold Out', 'Breakdown', 'Minimum wage', 'copy & paste', 'sign in', 'Silicon Valley', 'Best Buy', 'Login', 'AsyncMoveTask', 'testSerialization'.

A mixture: commas right after a title-like technical noun phrase at the start of a document ('Signal transduction inhibitors,', 'Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease,'), plus unrelated hits on ' from', 'ive', ' end', ' female', numbers and words in code.

Fires on the completing token of well-known technical names, commands and URL domains ('launchpad', 'SteamOS', 'git pull', 'git branch', 'apt-get install', 'purl.org', 'pastebin.com', 'MSBuild', 'TLSv'), and also on established multi-word names ('Champions League', 'Society of Automotive Engineers').

Fires on a sentence-initial subject pronoun 'We' (also 'They') that opens a methods sentence in a scientific or medical abstract ('We examined', 'we administered', 'They used'). It is much weaker on pronouns in other genres.

Fires on markup and command-syntax tokens that begin a command or close a tag: LaTeX backslashes ('\\usepackage', '^\\infty', '{\\'), docblock '@' (' @param'), and HTML closing tokens ('.</', '"></', '</').

Fires on the colon that separates a parameter name from its type in typed function signatures (Swift, Kotlin, TypeScript: 'indexPath: IndexPath', 'module: DModule'). Other colons fire weakly (journal citations 'Chem. 65:', 'Name:').
A mixture: ' under' in 'Licensed under the Apache License' file headers, breast/mammary words, email terms ('pop3', 'e-mail', '@' in an AMQP URI), and 'exterior algebra/power'.

Fires on end-of-sentence or trailing punctuation, especially exclamation marks and ellipses ('!', '...', '…', '[...') in promotional, informal or teaser text. Plain sentence-final periods are moderate to weak.
A mixture: nested ' namespace' in C++, 'xmlns:' colons in Android XML, build tags ('!gccgo'), decimal points and digits in clinical percentages, and assorted prose words.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word split into several tokens, mid-sentence, in any language ('ac'+usada, 'Pel'+áez, 'sp'+ats, 'ent'+hralling, 'conf'+ederates, 'ne'+oplasm, 'gr'+ansket). Whole-word tokens fire only weakly.

Fires on the final suffix piece of a multi-token technical word or identifier ('saphen'+'ous', 'frontotemp'+'oral', 'Cure'+'us', 'my'+'Ctrl') and on dots and pieces inside citation and file identifiers ('@pbio.1002412', 'core-3.0.4.jar').
Two jobs: ' to' after 'happens/happened' ('happens to be') and '-sectional' in 'cross-sectional study'. The other hits are weaker and scattered.

Strongest on ' software' in 'This program/code is free software' license headers (also 'Free Software Foundation'). Separately it fires on assorted mid-word completions (e'quest'rians, cro'cod'iles, Dop'pler', 'Auto-generated').
